name: Seraiah
overview: Seraiah was a male priest from the tribe of Levi, known particularly as the son of Hilkiah. He lived in Jerusalem, serving in a religious capacity during the time recorded in Nehemiah. His role as a priest highlights his involvement in the spiritual leadership of Israel in the city of Jerusalem.
namesAndTitles: The name Seraiah means 'YHWH persists,' 'YHWH is prince,' or 'YHWH contends,' reflecting a strong connection to the Lord. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:11, emphasizes the divine nature associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Seraiah was the son of Hilkiah, establishing his familial lineage within the priestly line. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Seraiah's significance lies in his priestly heritage and service in Jerusalem, marking him as part of the Levitical leadership during a critical period of Israel's history. His connection to Hilkiah situates him within a notable priestly family, contributing to the restoration and religious life of Jerusalem as noted in Nehemiah. His presence underscores the continuity of priestly duties and the faithfulness of God's covenant people in the post-exilic era.
